transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Gotcha, so day-to-day it feels like the front desk has things covered.  

When she steps away—lunch, sick days, on another call, or after hours—what usually happens to those calls?
User: We just call people back when we can. It's always worked out fine for us.
Agent: Totally hear you—if calling back has worked so far, there’s no urgency to change just to change.  

When you think about the last few months, have there been any calls where, by the time you called back, the person had already booked somewhere else or just disappeared?
User: Can't say for sure. We've never really counted misses. Feels like a solution looking for a problem.
Agent: Yeah, I get that—if you’re not feeling any real pain from it, it can totally sound that way.  

Let me ask you this: if one new booked job or customer a week came from catching calls you currently miss, would that actually move the needle for you, or would it be a drop in the bucket?
User: Well, I suppose catching even one more job could help, but I'm not convinced we miss that many.
Agent: Totally fair—that uncertainty is exactly where most people are.  

Right now, do you have any way of seeing how many calls hit voicemail or go unanswered in a typical week, or is it more of a “we assume it’s fine” situation?
User: We mostly assume it's fine. Janet's been here 9 years and handles calls well enough.
Agent: Totally makes sense—if Janet’s solid and it “feels” fine, you’re not staring at a problem.  

If your call volume doubled next month—busy season, promo, whatever—could Janet realistically handle that on her own, or would things start slipping?
User: If call volume doubled, it might get tight. Could use backup, but I’m still not entirely sold.
Agent: Totally fair, you sound pretty level‑headed about it and not in “emergency mode.”  

When things *do* get tight today—Janet on a call, someone at the counter, phone ringing again—what happens to that second or third caller right now?
User: They might end up leaving a message, or sometimes we just call them back when we get a chance.
Agent: Got it, so some hit voicemail and some you get back to when things slow down.  

If you could flip a switch so every one of those overflow callers either booked an appointment or told you exactly what they needed—without adding another person to payroll—would that be interesting to explore, or not really a priority right now?
User: That could be interesting as a backup layer. Alright, I can see the value. Go ahead and book your demo.
Agent: Got it, that makes sense—using it as a backup so nothing slips through.  

What’s your name, and what’s the best email to send the calendar invite to?
User: Dave Kowalski. You can send the invite to dkowalski@kowalskiautobody.com. Looking forward to seeing how this works.
Agent: Nice, thanks Dave.  

Last thing so I don’t waste your time—do you prefer something earlier in the day, like mid-morning, or later in the afternoon for the demo with Jay?
User: Mid-morning works best for me. Let’s aim for that. Thanks for setting this up.
Agent: Perfect, mid-morning it is.  

Do you usually have more breathing room closer to 9, 10, or 11 your time?
User: 10 AM usually works best for me. Let's go with that. Looking forward to it.
Agent: Nice, 10 AM it is.  

Are you generally better on, say, Tuesday or Thursday mornings, or is another day this week easier for you?
User: Tuesday morning at 10 AM sounds good. Appreciate you working with my schedule.
Agent: Perfect, Tuesday at 10 AM it is for a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay—he’ll show you how the backup layer actually catches those overflow calls and turns them into booked work.  

Is there anyone else from your team, like Janet or a manager, you’d want on that call, or is it just you for now?
User: Just me for now. I'll fill in Janet later if it looks promising. Thanks for setting it up.
Agent: Got it, just you on Tuesday and you’ll loop Janet in if it makes sense after. I’ll send that invite for Tuesday at 10 AM with Jay, it’ll be a 20‑minute, no‑commitment walkthrough so you can see exactly how the backup layer would work for you. Thanks for taking the time today, Dave—talk to you Tuesday!
